section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Papillon Journey is a JRPG-like, game-based online training platform in system and software engineering, where players advance their education and develop their engineering skills through quests, challenges, mini-games, and immersive storylines.
This document presents our vision for the project: what it is, why it matters, and how we plan to make it succeed.

section.title: Purpose
section.simpara: Formal and model-driven approaches to software development emerged in the 1960s–1980s through close collaboration between academia and industries operating under extreme safety and reliability demands — the earliest being defence, aerospace, nuclear power, and railway signalling. Their use broadened during the 1990s–2000s to other life-critical (automotive, medical devices) and high-stakes areas (finance, hardware design). They are now gradually entering unregulated, mainstream software engineering, finding applications in cloud infrastructure, telecommunications, blockchain, and cybersecurity.
Papillon Journey aims to build on this momentum by tackling three major hindrances to wider adoption:

listitem.simpara: Limited exposure: the historical confinement of these approaches to high-assurance projects has unintentionally reinforced the misconception that they are irrelevant to the daily concerns of most software professionals. Demonstrating their effectiveness through large-scale open-source initiatives in web, mobile, and game development will help dispel this view.

Inverted pedagogy: children learn to add and multiply long before they ever hear of ring theory — and only if they choose to. Yet formal modelling is typically taught the other way around: heavy on theory, light on practice, and illustrated with simplistic ‘toy examples’ that bear little resemblance to the challenges encountered in industry.

Fragmented tooling: companies favour tools that integrate seamlessly into existing workflows, but those supporting formal methods — narrowly specialised and rarely interoperable — often fail to do so. Chrysal Studio, the research subproject of Papillon Journey, will explore and prototype a unified integrated engineering environment to change that.
